meta.titre: Environmental Physics: Energy Sources, Greenhouse Effect and Ozone

sections.contenu_markdown: Cameroon has large rivers, strong sunshine in the north and plentiful biomass, yet many villages around Bertoua or Maroua still depend on a generator or kerosene lamp for hours every day. At the same time, burning fuel in generators and clearing forests adds carbon dioxide to the air, and refrigerators and old air conditioners release gases that harm the ozone layer. Environmental physics links the sources of energy, the energy we can obtain from them, and the effects of using them on the atmosphere. GCE Paper 2 asks for definitions, distinctions and consequences, and sometimes a short calculation of the power from the wind, water or the Sun.

items: Energy is conserved: it is transformed from one form to another and the total stays constant.
Power is the rate of transfer of energy, $P = E/t$, measured in watts ($1\ \mathrm{W} = 1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}$).
The kilowatt-hour is an energy unit: $1\ \mathrm{kWh} = 3.6\times10^{6}\ \mathrm{J}$.
Electromagnetic radiation includes infrared, visible light and ultraviolet; ultraviolet has shorter wavelength and higher photon energy than visible light.

sections.titre: Energy sources, efficiency and renewable power

variantes.quand_utiliser: Use it for questions that ask you to define or explain the greenhouse effect and its consequences.
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Definition.** The greenhouse effect is the warming of the lower atmosphere and the Earth's surface that occurs because certain gases absorb the infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and re-radiate part of it back towards the surface. Sunlight (mostly visible light of short wavelength) passes through the atmosphere and warms the ground. The ground emits **infrared** radiation of longer wavelength, which the **greenhouse gases** (water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, CFCs) absorb and re-emit in all directions, including downwards. Without this natural effect the mean surface temperature would be about $-18\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ instead of about $15\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The **enhanced** greenhouse effect is caused by human activities that increase the concentrations of these gases: burning fossil fuels, deforestation and livestock farming. **Consequences:** global warming, melting of ice caps and glaciers, rising sea level that floods coastal areas, more frequent droughts and extreme weather, and shifts in the regions where crops can grow.

variantes.quand_utiliser: Use it for questions on the ozone layer, CFCs and ultraviolet radiation.
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Definition.** Ozone depletion is the thinning of the ozone layer, the region of the stratosphere (roughly 15 to 35 km above the surface) that contains ozone $\mathrm{O_3}$ and absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun. The main cause is the release of **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, formerly used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays. In the stratosphere ultraviolet radiation breaks CFC molecules and releases chlorine atoms; each chlorine atom acts as a catalyst and destroys very many ozone molecules before it is removed. **Consequences:** more ultraviolet radiation reaches the surface, which increases the risk of skin cancer and cataracts, damages the immune system, reduces crop yields and harms plankton in the oceans. Ozone depletion and the greenhouse effect are different phenomena with different causes, although CFCs contribute to both.

variantes.nom: Fossil fuels, biofuels and the energy crisis
variantes.quand_utiliser: Use it when you must distinguish types of fuel or discuss why energy shortages persist.
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Fossil fuels** (coal, oil, natural gas) were formed over millions of years from the remains of plants and animals buried under heat and pressure. They are non-renewable, and burning them returns carbon that was stored underground to the atmosphere as carbon dioxide. **Biofuels** (ethanol from sugar cane or cassava, biodiesel from palm oil, biogas from animal waste) are produced from recently grown biomass. They are renewable on a short time scale, and the carbon dioxide released when they burn was recently absorbed by the plants, so the net addition to atmospheric carbon dioxide can be small. **Energy crisis in developing countries.** A country can have large energy resources and still have shortages because it lacks the capital, technology and infrastructure (power stations, transmission lines, refineries, roads) needed to convert and distribute energy; because of poor maintenance and losses in the network; because many people live in dispersed rural areas; and because low incomes limit the ability to pay for modern energy.

sections.contenu_markdown:
**Primary and secondary sources.** A **primary** source of energy is found in nature and is used as it occurs or after simple extraction: coal, crude oil, natural gas, uranium, sunlight, wind, flowing water, geothermal heat, biomass. A **secondary** source is produced by converting a primary source: electricity, petrol and diesel (refined from crude oil), hydrogen produced by electrolysis, charcoal made from wood. Energy sources are also **renewable** (replaced in a human lifetime: sunlight, wind, water, biomass) or **non-renewable** (finite stock: coal, oil, gas, uranium).

**Efficiency.** No energy conversion is perfectly efficient, because some energy is always transferred to the surroundings as thermal energy:

$$\text{efficiency} = \frac{\text{useful energy (or power) output}}{\text{total energy (or power) input}} \ (\times 100\%)$$

**Power available from renewable sources.** For the wind passing through a circle of area $A = \pi r^2$ swept by the blades, at speed $v$ and air density $\rho$:

$$P_{wind} = \tfrac12 \rho A v^3$$

so doubling the wind speed gives eight times the power. For water falling through a height $h$ with volume flow rate $Q$ (in $\mathrm{m^3\,s^{-1}}$), the power from a hydroelectric station of overall efficiency $\eta$ is

$$P = \eta\,\rho\, g\, h\, Q \qquad (\rho = 1000\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}} \text{ for water, } g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$$

For solar panels of area $A$ receiving intensity $I$ (in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$) with efficiency $\eta$, the electrical power is $P = \eta I A$. The Sun's intensity at the surface depends on the time of day, the weather and the angle of the panel, which is why solar and wind supplies need storage or a back-up. Use $\rho_{air} = 1.2\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ unless another value is given.

etapes.action: Calculate the area swept by the blades.
etapes.justification: The blades sweep out a circle whose radius is the blade length.

etapes.action: Calculate the power of the wind through this area.
etapes.justification: The kinetic energy carried by the moving air per second is $\tfrac12\rho A v^3$.

etapes.action: Apply the efficiency to find the electrical power.
etapes.justification: Only a fraction of the power in the wind is converted to electrical power.

etapes.action: Find the energy delivered in one day and the number of households.
etapes.justification: Energy in kilowatt-hours is power in kilowatts multiplied by time in hours.
etapes.resultat_markdown: $E = 135.11\times24 = 3243\ \mathrm{kWh}$ and the number of households is $\dfrac{3243}{5.0} = 649$

etapes.action: Use the cubic dependence on the wind speed.
etapes.justification: Since $P \propto v^3$, doubling $v$ multiplies the power by $2^3$.

sections.enonce_markdown: A wind turbine has blades of length $20\ \mathrm{m}$. The wind speed is $8.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and the density of air is $1.2\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. The overall efficiency of the turbine and generator is $35\%$. Calculate the power of the wind through the area swept by the blades, the electrical power output, and the energy delivered in 24 hours in kilowatt-hours. A household uses $5.0\ \mathrm{kWh}$ per day: how many households could be supplied? What happens to the power of the wind if the wind speed doubles?
sections.conclusion_markdown: The wind carries **386 kW** through the swept area, the turbine delivers **135 kW**, which is **3240 kWh** per day, enough for about **650 households**. Doubling the wind speed multiplies the available power by **8**, which is why wind farms are built where winds are strong and steady.

items.pourquoi_faux: These are two different phenomena. Ozone depletion lets more ultraviolet radiation reach the ground. The greenhouse effect comes from gases absorbing the infrared radiation emitted by the Earth.
items.erreur_markdown: Saying that the hole in the ozone layer causes global warming, or that the greenhouse effect is caused by the destruction of ozone.
items.correction_markdown: Greenhouse effect: infrared absorbed by greenhouse gases, consequence global warming. Ozone depletion: CFCs destroy ozone, consequence more ultraviolet radiation, with skin cancer and cataracts.

items.pourquoi_faux: The gases absorb and re-emit the infrared radiation from the warm Earth, not the incoming sunlight. The natural greenhouse effect keeps the planet warm enough for life; the problem is the enhanced effect caused by extra emissions.
items.erreur_markdown: "Greenhouse gases trap the Sun's rays so that they cannot leave, and the greenhouse effect is entirely harmful."
items.correction_markdown: Say that greenhouse gases absorb infrared radiation emitted by the surface and re-radiate part of it back, and distinguish the natural effect from the enhanced greenhouse effect.

items.pourquoi_faux: Electricity and petrol do not occur freely in nature in a usable form: electricity is produced by converting other energy, and petrol is refined from crude oil.
items.erreur_markdown: Listing electricity as a primary source of energy, or petrol as a primary source.
items.correction_markdown: Crude oil, coal, wind and sunlight are primary sources; electricity, petrol and hydrogen are secondary sources.

items.pourquoi_faux: Renewable and non-renewable refer to how fast the stock is replaced, not to pollution. Fossil fuels take millions of years to form, whereas biomass can regrow within a few years.
items.erreur_markdown: Defining biofuels as renewable "because they are natural" and fossil fuels as non-renewable "because they pollute".
items.correction_markdown: Fossil fuels: formed over millions of years from buried organisms, finite stock. Biofuels: made from recently grown plants or waste, replaceable on a short time scale.

items.pourquoi_faux: The kinetic energy per unit mass is $\tfrac12 v^2$, and the mass of air passing per second is $\rho A v$. The product contains $v^3$.
items.erreur_markdown: Forgetting the cube when calculating wind power, writing $P = \tfrac12\rho A v$ or $P = \tfrac12\rho A v^2$.
items.correction_markdown: Use $P = \tfrac12\rho A v^3$: a wind speed twice as large gives $8$ times the power.

items.enonce_markdown: A thermal power station receives $600\ \mathrm{MW}$ of power from burning fuel and delivers $210\ \mathrm{MW}$ of electrical power. (a) Calculate its efficiency. (b) Calculate the rate at which energy is wasted as thermal energy. (c) State whether electricity is a primary or a secondary source of energy and explain your choice.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Efficiency $= \dfrac{P_{out}}{P_{in}} = \dfrac{210}{600} = 0.35 = $ **35%**.

(b) Wasted power $= 600 - 210 = $ **390 MW**, transferred to the surroundings (cooling water and air) as thermal energy.

(c) Electricity is a **secondary** source: it is produced by converting the chemical energy of the fuel (a primary source), and it does not occur ready for use in nature.

items.enonce_markdown: Water falls through a height of $45\ \mathrm{m}$ at a hydroelectric station, with a flow rate of $12\ \mathrm{m^3\,s^{-1}}$. The overall efficiency is $80\%$. The density of water is $1000\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ and $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. (a) Calculate the electrical power output. (b) Calculate the energy produced in one day in megawatt-hours. (c) A village uses an average power of $300\ \mathrm{kW}$. How many such villages can be supplied?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $P = \eta\rho g h Q = 0.80\times1000\times9.8\times45\times12 = 4234000\ \mathrm{W} = $ **4.23 MW**.

(b) $E = P\,t = 4.23\ \mathrm{MW}\times24\ \mathrm{h} = $ **102 MWh** per day.

(c) Number of villages $= \dfrac{4234000}{300000} = 14.1$, so **14 villages** can be supplied (the whole number below 14.1).

items.enonce_markdown: A school needs a solar installation that delivers $9000\ \mathrm{W}$ of electrical power in full sunshine. The panels have an efficiency of $18\%$ and receive an intensity of $800\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ in full sunshine; the equivalent of $5.5$ hours of full sunshine occurs each day. (a) Calculate the area of panels required. (b) Each panel has an area of $1.6\ \mathrm{m^2}$: how many panels must be bought? (c) Calculate the electrical energy produced per day in kWh. (d) This energy would otherwise come from a diesel generator of efficiency $30\%$, using diesel that releases $36\ \mathrm{MJ}$ per litre. Calculate the volume of diesel saved per day.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $P = \eta I A$, so $A = \dfrac{P}{\eta I} = \dfrac{9000}{0.18\times800} = $ **62.5 m$^2$**.

(b) $\dfrac{62.5}{1.6} = 39.06$, so the number of panels must be rounded up to **40** panels.

(c) $E = 9.0\ \mathrm{kW}\times5.5\ \mathrm{h} = $ **49.5 kWh** per day.

(d) $49.5\ \mathrm{kWh} = 49.5\times3.6 = 178.2\ \mathrm{MJ}$ of electrical energy. The generator must take in $\dfrac{178.2}{0.30} = 594\ \mathrm{MJ}$ from the diesel, and the volume is $\dfrac{594}{36} = $ **16.5 litres** per day.

items_markdown: Primary sources occur in nature (coal, crude oil, sunlight, wind, uranium); secondary sources are made by converting them (electricity, petrol, hydrogen). Renewable means replaced on a short time scale.
Efficiency is useful output divided by total input; the rest is transferred as thermal energy. Wind: $P = \tfrac12\rho A v^3$. Hydro: $P = \eta\rho g h Q$. Solar: $P = \eta I A$.
Greenhouse effect: gases absorb the infrared radiation emitted by the Earth and re-radiate part of it downwards; the enhanced effect leads to global warming and sea-level rise.
Ozone depletion: CFCs release chlorine atoms that catalytically destroy ozone in the stratosphere, so more ultraviolet radiation reaches the surface, causing skin cancer and cataracts.
Do not confuse the greenhouse effect with ozone depletion: they have different causes and different consequences.
